pairs.locus: Paul the Deacon, Fabulae 1 (Leo aeger, vulpis et ursus), 57-62
pairs.question: Si vera refers, dulcissima vulpis, dic mihi, quid citius dixerit hic medicus?
pairs.answer: Ursino si te possum circumdare tergo, non mora, languor abit sanaque vita redit.
pairs.derivation: The lion (rex) genuinely asks the fox to report what the doctor prescribed (interrogative 'quid... dixerit'). I dropped the speech tag 'Rex quoque ait:'. The fox's reply opens with the non-answering preamble 'Cautius haec famulae suscipe verba tuae' (an exhortation to listen, not an answer), so per the skip-preamble rule I advanced the answer's start to the operative answering sentence 'Ursino si te possum circumdare tergo, non mora, languor abit sanaque vita redit' — the actual prescription. After this the narration resumes ('Continuo iussu domini distenditur ursus').

pairs.locus: Paul the Deacon, Fabulae 2 (Vitellus et ciconia), 78-81
pairs.question: Io frater, cur tristis pectore mugis, vel cur turbatus florida rura teris?
pairs.answer: Soror, est iam tertia nunc lux, quod lac non tetigi et famulentus eo.
pairs.derivation: The stork asks the calf why he is sad (double interrogative 'cur... cur'); I dropped the speech tag 'dicit'. The calf's reply directly answers the cause: it is the third day he has had no milk and goes hungry. I dropped the framing 'Cui sic respondit:'; 'Soror' is the calf's own vocative within the utterance and is kept contiguous. The answer ends at the full stop; what follows is the stork's next speech ('Verba refert ales...').
